case_scope: United Kingdom party finance, source-of-funds, foreign influence, and electoral-regulator powers

democratic_nondomination_gate.note: The UK has formal reporting and an active reform agenda, but the JCNSS/Rycroft review surface keeps source-of-funds, overseas donor resources, crypto/financial rails, party duties, and Electoral Commission powers open.

party_access_market.note: Nearly £65m accepted in 2025 makes aggregate transparency insufficient; the case needs donor concentration, event/access, candidate-level, and policy-domain linkage.

foreign_or_cross_border_political_financ.note: Official parliamentary and government-review sources identify foreign-finance routes and recommend stronger checks, but implementation and sanction outcomes are not yet proven.

political_finance_enforcement_capacity.note: Information powers over financial institutions, crypto platforms, and HMRC links are part of the proof burden; publication of a review is not enforcement conversion.

lobbying_register_quality.note: Political donations must be linked to lobbying, hospitality, advisory roles, think tanks, and procurement/regulatory outcomes before comfort scoring.

reform_countermobilization_risk.note: Reform success depends on enforceable due diligence and sanctions after review recommendations.

proof_debt: candidate-level surplus and local spending flows

gate_12_democratic_non_domination.why: Gate 12 is watch rather than pass: reporting exists, but source-of-funds verification, overseas/crypto routes, regulator powers, and party due-diligence outcomes remain open.
